questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on the right forearm with rolled, indurated edges and central black eschar. The lesion began as a pruritic papule 5 days ago. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis classically presents as a painless eschar (malignant pustule) with surrounding edema after contact with infected animals or soil. The black eschar and painless nature are hallmarks.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules with Wickham's striae on her wrists and ankles. Oral examination reveals a lacy white pattern on the buccal mucosa. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Lichen planus with characteristic Wickham's striae and oral lacy white patches is treated first-line with topical high-potency corticosteroids (e.g., clobetasol). Systemic therapy is reserved for extensive or recalcitrant disease.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with painless genital ulcer with a clean base and indurated edges. Dark-field microscopy reveals spirochetes. VDRL is reactive at 1:64. Which stage of syphilis does this represent?
questions.exp: Painless indurated ulcer (chancre) with positive dark-field microscopy is diagnostic of primary syphilis. VDRL positivity at 1:64 is consistent. Secondary syphilis presents with rash, condylomata lata, and systemic features after the chancre heals.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man from Bihar presents with hypopigmented patches on the trunk. Skin smear from the lesion edge shows acid-fast bacilli (AFB) on Wade-Fite stain. Histopathology shows foamy macrophages (Virchow cells) with numerous bacilli. The lepromin test is negative. What is the classification?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterized by numerous AFB on smear, foamy Virchow cells on histopathology, and negative lepromin test (indicating poor cell-mediated immunity). It is multibacillary leprosy.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with intensely pruritic burrows between finger webs, along the wrist flexures, and on the areolae. Multiple family members are similarly affected. Which treatment applied from neck to toe and left for 8 hours is first-line?
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is the first-line topical treatment for scabies. It is applied from neck to toe and washed off after 8-12 hours. It is effective, safe, and preferred over lindane (neurotoxicity risk) especially in children and pregnant women.

questions.q: A 55-year-old diabetic woman presents with painful tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin on the lower limbs. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae on normal or erythematous skin, predominantly in elderly patients. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. It is subepidermal with anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with extensive molluscum contagiosum lesions on the face. CD4 count is 80 cells/µL. The causative agent belongs to which family?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a member of the Poxviridae family. In HIV patients with low CD4 counts, extensive facial lesions are common and a marker of advanced immunodeficiency.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and arthritis. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous pattern). Anti-dsDNA is elevated. Complement C3 and C4 are low. What is the Sontheimer-Gilliam classification of her cutaneous manifestation?
questions.exp: The malar (butterfly) rash is the hallmark of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE). It is associated with active systemic disease, elevated anti-dsDNA, and low complement levels.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery micaceous scales on the extensor surfaces of elbows and knees. Nail pitting and oil-drop sign are present. Auspitz's sign is positive. Which cytokine is most central to the pathogenesis of this condition?
questions.exp: IL-17 (produced by Th17 cells) is central to the pathogenesis of psoriasis. It drives keratinocyte proliferation and neutrophil recruitment. Biologics targeting IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab) are highly effective in psoriasis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders and surface telangiectasia on the nose. It has been slowly growing for 2 years. Excision reveals palisading nuclei at the periphery of tumor islands with retraction artefact. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer, presenting as a pearly papule with rolled edges and telangiectasia. Histology shows palisading peripheral nuclei and retraction artefact (clefting between tumor nests and stroma).

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a dermatomal distribution on the right flank. She reports burning pain preceding the rash by 48 hours. Which antiviral should be started within 72 hours of rash onset?
opts: Either B or C are acceptable
questions.exp: Herpes zoster treatment within 72 hours reduces severity and duration. Valacyclovir 1g TID and famciclovir 500mg TID for 7 days are equally preferred due to better oral bioavailability and simpler dosing compared to acyclovir 800mg 5x/day.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with erythematous papules on the face (malar area, nasolabial folds) with scale and crusting. She has seborrheic dermatitis. A fungal organism is implicated. Which organism is primarily responsible?
questions.exp: Malassezia (formerly Pityrosporum) species, particularly M. globosa and M. restricta, play a central role in seborrheic dermatitis pathogenesis. These lipophilic yeasts produce irritating fatty acids that trigger inflammation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with deep-seated purplish nodules over the trunk. He is HIV positive with CD4 count of 50 cells/µL. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and plasma cell infiltrate. HHV-8 is positive. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma in AIDS is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV). It presents with purplish vascular nodules and histology shows spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces. It differs from bacillary angiomatosis (caused by Bartonella) which responds to antibiotics.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with a tender erythematous nodule on the anterior shin. She has recently started oral contraceptives. ESR is elevated. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Biopsy of the nodule shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum presents as tender pretibial nodules. It is a reactive condition (causes include sarcoidosis, OCPs, infections, IBD). Histology shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy suggests sarcoidosis as the trigger.

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with scaly, erythematous plaque on the face with central scarring and follicular plugging. The lesion has been present for 5 years. Biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, follicular plugging, vacuolar interface change, and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) presents as chronic scarring plaques with follicular plugging and central atrophy. Histology shows hyperkeratosis, follicular plugging, vacuolar interface change, and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate — the classic triad.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with grouped, pruritic vesicles symmetrically on elbows, knees, and buttocks. Jejunal biopsy shows subtotal villous atrophy. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. DIF shows granular IgA at BMZ (unlike linear IgA in LABD). It responds to dapsone and a gluten-free diet. Anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies are positive.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia, calcinosis cutis, and dysphagia. ANA is positive with anticentromere antibody pattern. What is this subset of systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) represents limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are its hallmark. It has a better prognosis than diffuse SSc.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma, what is the key advantage of this technique over standard wide local excision?
opts: Complete margin assessment allowing maximum tissue conservation
questions.exp: Mohs surgery allows complete circumferential peripheral and deep margin assessment (100% margin evaluation) in real-time, enabling tissue conservation while ensuring complete tumor removal. Standard WLE samples only 1-2% of margins.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with widespread urticaria and angioedema after taking aspirin. She has a history of nasal polyps and asthma. The mechanism responsible is:
opts: Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition causing arachidonic acid shunting to leukotriene pathway
questions.exp: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad: asthma, nasal polyps, NSAID sensitivity) occurs due to COX-1 inhibition, which shunts arachidonic acid to the 5-lipoxygenase pathway, increasing cysteinyl leukotrienes causing bronchoconstriction and urticaria.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man develops a crusted, honey-colored plaque on the face of his 5-year-old child after a cut. Which organism is the most common cause of non-bullous impetigo?
opts: Both GAS and S. aureus equally
questions.exp: While historically GAS was the main cause, Staphylococcus aureus is now the predominant cause of non-bullous impetigo. Bullous impetigo is caused exclusively by S. aureus phage group II producing exfoliative toxin.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with a soft, skin-colored, sessile papule with a central dell on the back of the neck. On dermoscopy, you see a white structureless area in the center with peripheral vessels. Histology shows proliferating follicular infundibulum. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dilated pore of Winer is a solitary follicular retention cyst with a wide patulous opening. Histology shows a markedly dilated infundibular cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium with radiating epithelial strands. It is benign and requires no treatment.

questions.q: A patient on long-term dapsone therapy for dermatitis herpetiformis presents with pallor, dark urine, and elevated methemoglobin levels. Which enzyme deficiency makes patients more susceptible to dapsone-induced haemolysis?
questions.exp: G6PD deficiency greatly increases susceptibility to dapsone-induced haemolytic anaemia and methemoglobinaemia. G6PD is critical for regenerating NADPH, which protects RBCs from oxidative stress caused by dapsone metabolites.

questions.q: A 19-year-old woman presents with erythema and pustules in a beard distribution. She shaves regularly. Gram stain of pustule contents shows Gram-positive cocci. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sycosis barbae is a chronic staphylococcal folliculitis of the beard area presenting with follicular pustules. Tinea barbae is fungal (shows hyphae on KOH). Pseudofolliculitis barbae occurs in curly-haired individuals from ingrown hairs, not from infection.

questions.q: A 55-year-old presents with pruritic, violaceous plaques with central clearing on the upper back. Histology shows mucin deposition, interstitial histiocytes, and lymphocytes in a 'busy' dermis pattern. Which disorder does this suggest?
questions.exp: Interstitial granulomatous dermatitis (IGD) presents with violaceous plaques showing 'busy dermis' histology with interstitial histiocytes, mucin, and lymphocytes. It is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and other autoimmune conditions.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with diffuse hair loss, positive pull test (>6 hairs), and exclamation mark hairs at the periphery. Family history is positive. Which immunological mechanism is responsible?
opts: Collapse of hair follicle immune privilege with CD8+ T cell attack
questions.exp: Alopecia areata results from collapse of the hair follicle immune privilege, with CD8+ NKG2D+ T cells attacking hair follicle melanocytes. The upregulation of IFN-γ and JAK-STAT signaling is central — explaining why JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, ritlecitinib) are effective.

questions.q: A 48-year-old man presents with multiple well-defined, reddish-brown plaques with fine scale on the trunk and proximal extremities. The plaques resolve with antibiotic therapy. Histology shows band-like lymphocytic infiltrate with plasma cells. PCR detects Borrelia burgdorferi DNA. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans (ACA) is late-stage Lyme disease caused by Borrelia afzelii, predominantly in Europe. It presents with inflammatory (bluish-red swelling) then atrophic skin changes on the extremities. Treatment is doxycycline for 28 days.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with erythema, scaling, and fissuring of her palms. She works as a hairdresser. Patch testing shows positive reaction to glyceryl monothioglycolate. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Glyceryl monothioglycolate in permanent wave solutions is a common cause of allergic contact dermatitis in hairdressers. Positive patch test confirms type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity. Irritant CD would show negative patch test.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing, flesh-colored, dome-shaped nodule with central keratin-filled crater on sun-exposed skin. The lesion appeared over 6-8 weeks. Histology shows a symmetric, well-differentiated squamous proliferation with central crater. What is this lesion?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing, self-resolving squamoproliferative lesion appearing in weeks. Histology shows a symmetric, crateriform architecture with central keratin plug and minimal atypia. Though classically considered benign, many now classify it as a variant of SCC.

questions.q: A patient with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis is started on methotrexate. After 3 months, LFTs show elevated transaminases. What is the recommended monitoring for hepatotoxicity in patients on long-term methotrexate?
opts: Liver biopsy after every 1 g cumulative dose
Procollagen III aminopeptide (PIIINP) levels and liver biopsy after 3.5-4 g cumulative dose
questions.exp: Current guidelines recommend serum PIIINP (procollagen III aminopeptide) as a non-invasive marker of hepatic fibrosis. Liver biopsy is recommended after every 1-1.5g cumulative dose or when PIIINP is persistently elevated. LFTs alone are unreliable for fibrosis detection.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with a targetoid lesion — central dusky erythema with a pale ring and outer red ring — on the palms and forearms, appearing 2 weeks after starting phenytoin. Mucous membranes are involved. She has fever and conjunctivitis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is defined by mucosal involvement plus epidermal detachment involving <10% BSA. Targetoid lesions, fever, and mucosal erosions after phenytoin exposure are classic. SJS/TEN spectrum is based on % BSA detachment: SJS <10%, overlap 10-30%, TEN >30%.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with verrucous, warty plaques on the lower leg with black dots on the surface. KOH preparation shows sclerotic (Medlar) bodies. What is the causative agent?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic subcutaneous mycosis most commonly caused by Fonsecaea pedrosoi. The pathognomonic finding is muriform (sclerotic/Medlar) bodies — dark, thick-walled, septate cells seen in tissue. Verrucous plaques on the lower limbs in farmers are classic.
